ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, every proposed director, shareholder, and UBO must be screened against the consolidated EU financial sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list, Luxembourg Ministry of Finance and CSSF sanction notices, and the national PEP registry maintained pursuant to AMLD 4/5. Senior foreign political figures, their family members, and close associates must be treated as enhanced-risk PEPs, requiring documented source of wealth, source of funds, and ongoing transaction monitoring. The AML/CFT professional must retain the screening report and risk classification for at least five years after termination of the business relationship. For third-country UBOs and non-EU corporate shareholders, country risk rating and adverse-media screening are mandatory.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), available at https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The RCS accepts company names in French, German, and Luxembourgish as the operating languages of the register. Names using non-Latin scripts must be translated and transliterated into Latin characters. For a Société à Responsabilité Limitée, the name must be accompanied by the legal-form identifier 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée', 'S.à r.l.', or 'SARL' where required by law and on all corporate documents. The proposed name must be distinctive, not misleading, and must not create confusion with an existing entity registered in the RCS.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS rejects the proposed name, the incorporating counsel or notary may file a written remedial clarification or a materially changed name through the LBR portal within ten working days from the rejection notice. If the rejection is maintained, a formal administrative appeal may be lodged with the Minister of Justice within one month, setting out the distinctiveness and non-confusion grounds. Where the ministerial decision remains adverse, judicial review may be sought before the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg within three months. During the appeal, a new and materially distinct name application may be filed for parallel clearance without prejudice to the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A standalone virtual office is not acceptable as the registered office of a Luxembourg SARL. The RCS requires a genuine physical address in Luxembourg where the company is lawfully administered, statutory records are kept, and official correspondence is received. A virtual mailbox may only support an already valid registered office and physical commercial substance. For a wholesale copper cathode trading company, reliance on a virtual office without personnel or trading records creates a high risk of UBO recharacterization, substance challenge, and administrative sanctions.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 40% during the first 24 months for a newly formed SARL with non-EU shareholders and physical-commodity trading scope. The risk falls to approximately 15% where the company uses a supervised Luxembourg domiciliation agent, maintains a dedicated office suite, and retains the full UBO/KYC file on site. Unannounced inspections may be carried out by the RCS, the Luxembourg tax administration, and customs authorities in coordination with AML/CFT supervisors.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 710-1 to 710-26 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and Accounting Records
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Register of Commerce and Companies (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Deed of incorporation (acte de constitution) and coordinated articles of association, submitted via the RCS online filing portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital is EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and paid up in cash. The capital must be deposited into a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) with a Luxembourg credit institution until the company is registered; the deposit certificate is filed with the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the initial shareholders hereby subscribe for and accept the full share capital of EUR 12,000, divided into 100 shares of EUR 120 each, and acknowledge that the amount has been deposited into a blocked escrow account; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is adopted and established at [Registered Office Address], Luxembourg; FURTHER RESOLVED, that Mr. [Name], an authorised natural person, is appointed as Manager (Gérant) of the Company with sole signatory power for the purposes of the Company’s registered operations, and that the deed of incorporation, as drafted, is hereby approved and authorized for submission to the Luxembourg Business Registers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and drafting of articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online name reservation; Luxembourg notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Reserve the company's legal name through the RCS online portal. Engage a Luxembourg notary to draft the articles of association (statuts) and the deed of incorporation, verifying the identity and legal capacity of all initial shareholders and managers. Ensure the name reservation remains valid until the filing is completed.
required_dossiers: Copy of identity documents of each shareholder and manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is refused, select an alternative name and reapply online. If the notary identifies legal issues in the draft, amend the clauses and resubmit accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit and blocked account certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) chosen by the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) in the name of the company in formation. Transfer the full minimum paid-up capital of EUR 12,000 to this account. Instruct the bank to issue a deposit certificate (attestation de blocage) addressed to the notary, confirming that the funds are held and will be released only upon RCS registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional AML/KYC documentation, promptly supply the information and ensure the certificate reflects the exact statutory capital amount.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalise the notarial deed of incorporation before the notary. All shareholders and managers must sign in person or by valid proxy. The notary verifies the capital deposit certificate, the legality of the articles, and the identity and professional eligibility of the managers. The notary then transmits the deed to the RCS.
required_dossiers: Deposit certificate for the blocked capital
Original identification documents or certified copies
Proof of address for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deed is refused, the notary will issue a written statement of defects; the parties correct the defect and reschedule the execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and registration with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS online filing portal, Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the notarial deed, coordinated articles, list of managers, and deposit certificate through the RCS e-file portal. Pay the statutory filing fee. After registration, the RCS issues the certificate of registration (certificat d'inscription) and assigns the company's registration number (matricule).
required_dossiers: Acceptance of office by the managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS registration is queried, the applicant receives a formal notice; deficiencies can be corrected and the filing resubmitted. An appeal may be filed with the District Court if the query is contested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication and post-registration tax and social security formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RESA publication), Administration de l'enregistrement, Administration de la TVA, and Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS automatically publishes the legal extract in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA) after registration. Within fifteen days of incorporation, register for corporate income tax, VAT, and municipal business tax with the Administration des Contributions Directes and the Administration de la TVA. Enroll the company and its managers with the CCSS for social security.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or social security registration is delayed, contact the relevant administration to rectify missing information; due to strict deadlines, proactive escalation is advisable to avoid penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial operating license is required for wholesale trading and physical arbitrage of non-ferrous copper cathodes under Luxembourg law. If a warehouse is operated, the Ministry of Economy and the Inspectorate of Labour and Mines (ITM) have advisory oversight.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating license is required for the commercial trading activity. A municipal establishment authorization may be needed only if physical warehousing or storage facilities are operated, in which case the relevant commune issues the permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, du Climat et de la Biodiversité (Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: No EIA required for the trading activity. Any future warehouse project would be screened under Annex II of the Luxembourg environmental impact assessment legislation and may require a simplified impact study depending on size and location.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For any storage site, compliance with the Luxembourg Water Management Act (Loi modifiée du 19 décembre 2008 sur l'eau) and the Waste Management Act (Loi du 21 mars 2012 relative aux déchets) is required. No contaminated process water may be discharged; surface water runoff must meet the thresholds of the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 27 July 2018 on wastewater discharge. VOC emissions from packaging or handling are minimal but any solvent-based operations must comply with industrial emissions regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the registered office, no specific fire safety certification is required. Should warehousing be established, the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) must issue a fire safety clearance after inspection. The Inspectorate of Labour and Mines (ITM) requires compliance with occupational health and safety standards, structural load limits, and the posting of consolidated internal regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration, for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDTV) – Luxembourg Indirect Tax Administration, for VAT registration and collection. Primary e-portal: MyGuichet.lu; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) for RCS registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned SARL must first be registered in the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) through Luxembourg Business Registers, obtaining a Luxembourg registration number. Thereafter, the entity must apply for a national business tax number (matricule d'impôt) from the ACD via the local Registration Tax Office. For VAT, the SARL must file Luxembourg VAT registration form (Formulaire 394) with the AEDTV, disclosing the expected turnover, ISIC activity codes, and bank details, to obtain a VAT identification number formatted with the LU prefix followed by numeric digits. No bank account or prior capital proof is required for registration, but non-resident directors must provide a local criminal record extract.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. However, a resident parent SARL may elect, jointly with resident group companies, to form an integrated tax regime (intégration fiscale) for corporate income tax and municipal business tax purposes, requiring a 95% direct or indirect participation and a minimum five-year commitment. For VAT purposes, financially and economically closely related persons may elect to form a VAT group (assujetti unique) under Article 60 of the Luxembourg VAT Act. Hybrid mismatch rules under EU/ATAD do not allow elective opt-in; entities are required to deny deductions or include income automatically in the case of hybrid mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for goods and services under the small business exemption. Cross-border intra-EU acquisitions and imports are subject to mandatory VAT registration irrespective of this threshold. For intra-EU distance sales of goods, the threshold is EUR 10,000; for distance sales of electronic services, the union threshold also is EUR 10,000. A wholesale copper-trading SARL engaged in intra-EU acquisitions or exports is required to register for VAT regardless of turnover because of its cross-border trading activity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently impose a general B2B real-time electronic invoicing, fiscal clearance, or digital stamping obligation. Electronic invoices are legally accepted provided authenticity and integrity are ensured, e.g., through EDI or advanced electronic signatures. Since 2025, public-sector invoices (B2G) must be submitted through the PEPPOL network using EN 16931 compliant e-invoices. No continuous transaction controls or real-time API clearance are in place.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The SARL may apply the 0% VAT rate for supplies of copper cathodes physically exported outside the EU or shipped to another EU Member State where the recipient is a taxable person holding a valid EU VAT number. For export outside the EU, the seller must provide documentary proof that the goods were transported outside the EU within the required time limits, ordinarily 90 to 90 days. For intra-EU supplies, the supplier must state the customer's VAT registration number on the invoice and demonstrate that the goods have been dispatched to the destination Member State. The export zero-rating also covers ancillary transport, packaging and freight services linked to the exported goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EX-A form / AES electronic export declaration)
Bill of Lading or CMR or Air Waybill evidencing physical movement of goods
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by the banking channel
Commercial invoice showing zero-rated sale and stating the VAT exemption law
Purchase contract and order documentation confirming the underlying copper trade
LME warrant transfer documentation or warehouse receipt evidencing copper cathode delivery
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDTV and Customs authorities may conduct retrospective audits generally within a three-year limitation period, extendable to ten years in cases of suspected VAT fraud or tax evasion. If the SARL cannot substantiate export zero-rating with the prescribed export declaration, movement evidence, transport document, and repatriation proof, VAT at the standard rate (17%) is immediately assessed. Default interest of 0.6% per month is applied, plus a late-payment penalty up to 10%. Administrative fines in serious or fraudulent cases can reach EUR 250,000, and criminal prosecution is possible if falsified export documentation is established. Inward Remittance Certificates and bank ledger entries are systematically checked to ensure that export proceeds are repatriated to the SARL within the 180-day benchmark; failure to evidence repatriation triggers a rebuttable presumption of a taxable domestic sale and reassessment with interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) together with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for financial conduct and prudential oversight; exchange control within the EU/EMU framework is governed by the BCL and the ECB for policies affecting cross-border capital flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a full member of the Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) and the eurozone; the euro (EUR) is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions, subject only to EU/EEA anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, sanctions screening, and CSSF/BCL supervisory reporting obligations. Profit remittance hurdles are minimal: a Luxembourg SARL may distribute dividends if the annual accounts do not show net assets below the subscribed capital plus non-distributable reserves (Luxembourg law on commercial companies Art. 710-1), and dividends, liquidation proceeds, or branch profits may be freely transferred cross-border subject to withholding tax (15% domestic; reduced under tax treaties or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, with potential 0% where conditions are met) and standard bank attestation of compliance. There are no exchange quotas, prior administrative approvals, or surrender requirements for current transactions, but transactions routed via any EUR correspondent or settlement account must include compliant SWIFT purpose codes and underlying trade documentation to satisfy BCL statistical reporting (Balance of Payments reporting) and CSSF AML/KYC checks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Luxembourg imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. All export proceeds in EUR or other convertible currencies may be retained in corporate bank accounts and used for treasury purposes; however, transactions exceeding EUR 10,000 (or equivalent) must be reported to the Cellule de Renseignement Financier (CRF) in line with AML obligations, and Cross-Border Payments Regulation or CSSF/BCL balance-of-payments reporting may require statistical declaration of a resident SARL's receipts/payments to non-residents. For physical copper cathode wholesale trading, the operative compliance focus is the availability of original commercial documentation (invoices, bills of lading, warehouse warrants, LC/MT103 records) and sanctions/embargoes screening rather than any FX conversion mandate.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Wealth and Commodity Trade Finance Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate feasibility with an EU/EEA e-money institution (EMI) or payment institution licensed under PSD2 and authorised in another EEA state, passporting into Luxembourg under the EU single passport. Practical legal constraints: (i) the EMI must be registered with the CSSF for Luxembourg activity and must comply with the revised Payment Services Act 2009 (as amended) and the e-money regime; (ii) most commercial banks require a traditional banking relationship for high-value physical commodity settlements; EMIs are generally unsuitable as the sole clearing rail for documentary LC operations involving copper cathodes, owing to restricted trade-finance capabilities and lower limits on transaction sizes; (iii) an EMI can only serve as an auxiliary e-wallet or FX conversion gateway for small-value payments, with segregation of client funds and safeguarding obligations under CSSF/EMD rules; (iv) user-obligation screening under sanctions and AML (5th and 6th EU Anti-Money Laundering Directives) applies, and the commodity trading counterparty profile must be demonstrably transparent. Overall feasibility rating: Low-Medium for core liquidity clearing, Medium for ancillary FX and vendor payments; any EMI arrangement should be ring-fenced and accompanied by a tier-1 correspondent-backed account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Luxembourg SARL, at least one authorised signatory (typically a manager/gérant, director, or ultimate beneficial owner with sufficient proof of identity and authority) must ordinarily attend a physical onboarding meeting at the bank's office in Luxembourg. Remote onboarding is permitted under Luxembourg AML law when a fully compliant video-identification solution is used and the bank has implemented secure electronic verification procedures; in practice, tier-1 banks such as BGL BNP Paribas, BCEE, BIL and ING Luxembourg will require either (i) a physical visit to the Luxembourg branch or (ii) a notarised/legalised signatory meeting followed by certified true copies and a bank-conducted video conference. For a newly incorporated SARL, banks generally insist on the physical appearance of the manager/UBO before opening high-value operational or trade-finance accounts, because the copper wholesale segment is classified as Medium-Risk Enhanced. Remote onboarding is possible only if the UBO and manager are already known to the bank, are located in a low-risk jurisdiction, and produce apostilled corporate documents (RC registre de commerce extract, articles of association, statutory business permit or nil-licence statement, UBO register extract, audited/starting balance sheet, and board resolution).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity in the ownership chain or identification of an intermediary shareholder without a clear economic rationale
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO register extract (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) not older than 3 months; corporate chart from RC Luxembourg; signed declaration of indirect ownership percentages; explanation memorandum for each non-Luxembourg parent/intermediate entity; audited financial statements of the immediate shareholder or, for newly formed structures, notarised certificate of good standing from foreign registry; legal opinions confirming no bearer shares or nominee arrangements contrary to Luxembourg law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or commodity-trading-intensive transaction flows with significant non-resident counterparties (particularly jurisdictions with perceived sanctions/AML risk)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed 12-month projected transaction flow schedule; executed master trading agreements or MTN contracts for non-ferrous metal purchases/sales; proforma invoices listing HS/CN code 7403 refined copper cathodes; LME membership or counterparty LME warrant statements; complete beneficial-owner and KYC packs for all direct material counterparties; sanctions/PEPS screening results for all counterparties and associated vessels/warehouses; explanation of trade purpose codes (e.g., T103 goods for processing/purchase) and proposed settlement rail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicion of trade-based money laundering due to price deviations or triangular payments (invoice from one party, payment instruction from another)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent commodity price benchmark evidence (LME Copper Grade A export settlement price, official LME closing quotations or Fastmarkets/Metal Bulletin copper cathode assessment) for each proposed transaction; original contract with Incoterms and delivery terms; warehouse delivery order and LME warrant transfer evidence; customs declaration (DUA/importer-export declaration or Intrastat) and transport/carriage documents (bill of lading/CRO); audit trail showing payment beneficiary corresponds to documented trade party and invoice reference; valuation report from an independent chartered commodity surveyor where price tolerance exceeds reasonable benchmarks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction volume/velocity inconsistent with a SARL's capital base, or rapid in-and-out wire movements (pass-through risk)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan with capital adequacy demonstration; shareholder capital injection evidence (paid-up share capital no less than EUR 12,000 for SARL); intercompany funding agreements with arm's-length interest; warehouse/wholesale trade finance lines committed by a bank or commodity trade financier; treasury policy documenting segregation of operational vs. escrow vs. trade-finance accounts; ageing reports of trade receivables/payables and physical inventory movements; independent confirmations from shipping brokers for non-financial trade substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Luxembourg financial administration flags unexplained deposits of cash-like instruments or digital-asset-linked liquidity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth documentation for each contributing shareholder and each trading counterparty; bank statements of originating accounts (redacted only to unrelated information); notarised or incriminating-free acquisition documents for the copper inventories; confirmation no crypto/stablecoin FX bridges are used; executed correspondent banking attestation covering all payment rails; legal opinion that transactions are uniformly reflected in VAT/income tax filings and no bearer or bearer-warrant-like artefacts are introduced.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-triggered rejection through EU/OFAC screening of counterparty, end-user, vessel, or warehouse (e.g., Russian aluminium/copper exposure, Iranian or North Korean counterparties)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dow Jones/Refinitiv/World-Check or equivalent real-time sanctions screening reports on all legal persons, natural persons, vessels, and warehouse addresses; OFAC and EU sanctions lists (incl. Annexes to EU Regulations 833/2014 and 269/2014) reviewed within 48 hours of each transaction; compliance manual with sanctions-blocking protocols and jurisdiction risk matrix; subordination certificate that the SARL will not act as an intermediary for sanctioned products; contractual 'Sanctions/Embargoes' clauses with indemnities from counterparties; evidence of physical-vessel TMSA/IMOSEA due diligence for shipping routes via sanctioned transshipment ports.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections into the Luxembourg SARL at formation or via subsequent increase must be handled by SWIFT MT103/MT202 transfers from the shareholder's bank account to the SARL's dedicated bank account in Luxembourg, with the exact purpose code 'T101' or 'EQUITY' and reference to the notarial deed or board resolution approving the capital increase; the bank will verify source of wealth. For loans/shareholder advances, use purpose code 'T101' or 'T112' (loans between non-financial corporations) and execute a formal intercompany loan agreement with commercial-rate interest. ECB Regulation 1745/2011 as integrated into EU statistical rules requires the bank to encode the transaction classification; the SARL should ensure the account field states 'CAPITAL INCREASE LU SARL' and provide the CSSF/BCL statistical reporting code A, category 'direct investment — other capital', if the shareholder is non-resident. No prior exchange control authorisation is required in Luxembourg, but the transfer must not be routed through or via sanctioned financial institutions or the Republic of Belarus/Russia/Syria/Iran/Crimea, and the bank will perform cascade checks and OFAC/EU sanction screening on both remitter and beneficiary before crediting. Any contribution in kind (e.g., copper cathode inventory or warrants) must be evidenced by a contribution-in-kind valuation approved by a Luxembourg chartered auditor or statutory auditor, with the deed filed with the Luxembourg trade register and public registry (RCS) and the contribution registered on the Luxembourg operational account or LME warrant custody account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Principal clearing rails for outbound trade settlements are (i) SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfers for open-account payments to vendors; (ii) MT202 cover instructions for nostro/loro correspondent settlements when the vendor uses a different bank; (iii) documentary letters of credit (LC) issued by the Luxembourg bank or by a confirming bank under UCP 600, with SWIFT MT700/MT707 issuance/amendment; (iv) LME warrant transfers via approved LME warrant service providers and custodian banks for delivery of Grade A copper cathodes against LC or warrant transfer plus SWIFT payment; and (v) for intra-group treasury centralisation, MT101/MT910/MT940 cash-management messages aligned with the CSSF transfer-pricing practices. All outgoing transfers require ISO 20022 or current SWIFT transaction reference with the correct EU Import/Export purpose code (e.g., T103 for purchase of goods, T210 for trading of commodities, or T111 for foreign exchange transactions as applicable), underlying invoice/contract, transport document, and, for value-dated LC settlement, the presentation of a compliant bill of lading and certificate of origin (where applicable). Liquidity clearing is optimised by concentrating EUR balances in a Luxembourg cash concentration account and executing cross-border vendor payments via SEPA or TARGET2 for euro transactions and via correspondent banks via SWIFT for non-euro transactions (USD, CNY, CHF). Trade disbursements connected to LME warrant deliveries should anchor in the physical warehouse location and settle through the LME clearing chain (LME Clear Ltd), with payment against delivery warrant transfer via a documentary LC or cash-against-documents arrangement; the Luxembourg bank must be provided with the warehouse receipt and warrant value to evidence economic substance under AML and BEPS compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD and EUR/CNH forwards (plain vanilla forward foreign exchange contracts) for up to a 12-month tenor
Rolling EUR/USD foreign exchange swaps (swap of principal and interest/cash flows for intercompany and trade settlements)

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing restricted or low-convertibility currencies that counterparties may require where ordinary deliverable forwards are unavailable, subject to Luxumbourg bank credit lines and counterparty ISDA/CSA documentation
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CIRS/CCS) between EUR and USD for hedging a financed copper-cathode inventory position
FX options (plain vanilla European call/put options) on EUR/USD or EUR/CNH, purchased to hedge trade payables/receivables without speculative intent

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual financial statements (dépôt des comptes annuels) with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), including management report and auditors' report when applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS/Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) through the eJustice portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after shareholder approval; approval must occur within 6 months of the financial year-end. For calendar-year companies, filing deadline is no later than 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Persistent non-filing triggers summons by the Public Prosecutor, court-ordered injunction with daily penalty (astreinte), and ultimately administrative strike-off (radiation) of the SARL from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owner information (confirmation RBE) - Retain and validate the identity of the ultimate beneficial owner(s)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per calendar year, generally within one month after the anniversary of the last confirmation or initial RBE filing; any shareholding or UBO change must be updated within one month of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory penalty of EUR 500 to EUR 5,000 per non-confirmation; repeated or wilful default may raise penalties to EUR 25,000 and/or imprisonment of directors for up to 6 months.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Convening and documentation of the Annual General Meeting (AGM) approving the annual accounts, allocation of profit, and discharge of the managers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office / SARL corporate records (not filed with the RCS but a statutory prerequisite)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be held within 6 months of the close of the financial year; for calendar-year accounting, AGM must occur no later than 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the AGM or approve annual accounts within the statutory period renders directors liable to civil damages; absence of a timely filing can independently trigger the RCS strike-off procedure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) if the SARL exceeds at least two of three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, annual average of 50 employees. Public-interest entities and companies in regulated financial sectors are always subject to audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP in compliance with the Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial and companies register and annual accounts (EU Accounting Directive transposition); IFRS as endorsed by the EU is optional for statutory individual accounts and mandatory for listed groups/consolidated statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must file and thereafter annually re-confirm the accurate beneficial ownership details in the Luxembourg RBE. The annual confirmation follows the anniversary date of the prior RBE declaration and any transfer of shares must be recorded in the shareholders register and reflected in the RBE within one month.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 3,000 - 9,000 (typical Luxembourg registered office / corporate agent annual fee for a wholesale trading SARL)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - 30,000 (typical certified audit fee for a medium-scale base-metals wholesale company with international documentation requirements)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined headline rate for Luxembourg City: 17% Corporate Income Tax (IRC) on taxable income exceeding EUR 175,000, 15% on the first EUR 175,000, plus 7% solidarity surcharge on the IRC, plus 6.75% Municipal Business Tax (MBT) on the business tax base, with MBT deductible for IRC purposes.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP-Box regime: 80% exemption of qualifying intellectual property income, producing an effective rate of approximately 5.19%; R&D tax credit; investment tax credit; 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains; EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief; unlimited loss carryforward for losses incurred from fiscal year 2017.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited for losses incurred from fiscal year 2017 onward; 17-year limitation for losses arising before fiscal year 2017 (Art. 110 LIR).
